title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad
content:
Goal: Track reproducer + root-cause hypotheses for recurring 401/429 spikes seen by internal and customer requests.

Summary of incidents:
- 2026-03-01 10:12 UTC: Customer X reported intermittent 401s for text-generation calls (~2% of requests over 30m).
- 2026-03-01 10:15 UTC: Internal p95 token latency spike followed by an increase in 429s from proxy layer.
- 2026-03-02 02:05 UTC: Cron job for metrics-exporter started hitting service account quota -> 429s cascaded to other tenants for a short window.

Commands tried / repro steps (local):
- curl reproduce (simple):
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/base-1","input":"hi"}' \
    https://api.redwood-inference.local/v1/generate
  -> sometimes returns 401 with body: {"error":"unauthorized","reason":"invalid_token"} (header: WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api")

- curl to token introspection (ok):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://auth.internal/v1/introspect
  -> 200 {"active":true,"exp":1710000000}  (token appears valid when introspected)

- Replayed production headers via mitm proxy to dev cluster: same 401 pattern when concurrent QPS > 200

- Rate-limit repro: high QPS loop (simulates client):
  for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood/base-1","input":"x"}' https://api...; done
  -> observed 429s starting around iteration ~320 (per-IP token-bucket triggered at proxy layer)

Error snippets seen in logs:
- proxy-gateway: 401 returned to client, upstream responded 200 -> mismatch in auth mapping (possible header stripping):
  "upstream_status=200 downstream_status=401 reason=auth-mismatch header-missing=x-requested-with"

- auth-service: "token_revoked check passed for token id=abcd1234" (this log is misleading, debug-level shows token introspection success)

- quota-service: "rate_limit_exceeded tenant=customer-x scope=global qps=350 limit=300"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Token caching/invalidation race: short-lived rotation of API keys (customer rotated API key but some pods still using old key due to env var cache) -> leads to sporadic 401s until rollout completed. Evidence: customer reported key rotation same time as first spike.
2) Proxy header rewrite bug at high concurrency: auth header or forwarded tenant header intermittently stripped when proxy threadpool saturates -> upstream sees unauthenticated request and returns 401. Evidence: upstream logs 200 but client sees 401; header-missing observed.
3) Global quota enforcement bump: noisy neighbors (metrics-exporter or internal crawler) triggered global limiter causing 429s; some 429s bubbled as 401 due to error mapping in gateway (bad mapping). Evidence: quota-service logs and cron timing.
4) Clock skew / token expiry rounding edge-case: tokens with very short TTL get considered expired by some nodes if clocks off by >5s. Low-confidence.

Notes / observations:
- Introspection returns active for tokens that clients get 401 on when called at same time -> suggests problem is between proxy and auth mapping, not token store.
- Repro needs both high concurrency and a particular header combination (x-tenant-id + x-request-id).
- Some older nginx ingress versions had bug with large header sets and worker process reloads -> check ingress version on nodes that handled failures.

Immediate next steps (todo):
- [ ] Add debug-level logging to proxy for header dump on 401/429 (include hashed token id, tenant header, request-id). Low-risk, roll to canary group. (Aisha)
- [ ] Correlate request_ids in gateway logs with upstream logs for a sample window (2026-03-01T10:00-10:30). (Michael)
- [ ] Check recent deploys for env var reload behavior (did we roll API_KEY_CONFIG or sidecar recently?). (me)
- [ ] Throttle/disable non-critical cron jobs (metrics-exporter) in staging to see effect on global quota. (infra)
- [ ] Add metric: fraction_of_401_with_upstream_200 for quick alerting. (observability)

Longer-term mitigations:
- Implement handshake verify: gateway should refuse to map upstream 200->downstream 401; instead return upstream payload for easier debugging.
- Harden header-forwarding under load, bump ingress or switch to envoy with consistent header semantics.
- Provide guidance to customers on safe key rotation patterns (grace window + dual-key support).

Quick links and references:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/12345/Auth+Rate+Limits+Runbook
- JIRA: ENG-4123 (investigate 401/429 patterns)
- Slack thread: #infra-auth (03/01)

Notes to self: keep this doc as ephemeral scratchpad. If root-cause confirmed, move summary to confluence and update runbook.

Random/log snippets to copy to ticket:
- "client=customer-x request_id=abc123 downstream=401 upstream=200 token_hash=sha256:abcd..."
- "quota-service: rate_limit_exceeded tenant=customer-x window=60s consumed=350 limit=300"

End of scratchpad.
